localBiteReport: As of the week of October 30–November 5, 2026, redfish are the most reliable inshore target on Choctawhatchee Bay, with schools actively feeding around bridges, jetties, and East Pass despite the lingering effects of a recent hurricane; live bait including pinfish, croakers, and herring has been most effective. Speckled trout in the 22–27-inch range are also showing up where anglers can locate concentrations of bait, though an unsettled fall transition — warm spells, the hurricane, and brief fronts — has kept trout and redfish somewhat scattered between their summer and winter locations; a sustained cool-down with overnight temps in the 50s is expected to tighten up the trout bite. It's also the tail end of the annual flounder run (peak: late October through mid-November), making Destin Pass and Mid-Bay Bridge structure worth targeting for migrating flounder on live finger mullet or mud minnows. Water temperature as of today is 76°F. Sheepshead and black drum should begin picking up around bridge pilings and jetties as water temperatures continue to cool into November.
